title: Claims of 'no difference' or 'no effect' in Cochrane and other systematic reviews
author: PRM Smith et al. (2020)
organization: PMC / NIH National Library of Medicine
snippet: Survey of 460 Cochrane reviews: no difference or no effect was claimed in abstracts of 36 (7.8%) reviews - many not justified by the data. Critical for testing NEGATIVE-claim parsing and over-claiming detection.
notes: Directly about no effect claims in systematic reviews - perfect NEGATIVE-findings source.

title: Natural experiments: A Nobel Prize awarded research design
author: FJM Molengracht-Arrega et al. (2022)
organization: PMC / NIH National Library of Medicine
snippet: Discusses natural experiments as causal-inference research designs evaluated retrospectively and prospectively using external shocks or factors. Methodological article on distinguishing CAUSAL from CORRELATIONAL claims.  Covers launches, Earth observation, human spaceflight, navigation, and technology programmes with budget and operational milestones.
notes: PMC peer-reviewed methodological article on natural experiments.

title: Estimating causal effects: considering three alternatives to regression
author: S O'Neill et al. (2016)
organization: PMC / NIH National Library of Medicine
snippet: Difference-in-differences (DiD) methods identify causal effects by contrasting change in outcomes pre- and post-intervention for treatment and comparison groups. Covers DiD, synthetic control, IV - 330+ citations.  OECD long-form 268-page report; multi-country GDP and inflation forecasts through 2025-2026 with country notes and policy analysis chapters.
notes: Cited 330+ times; econometrics causal-inference methodology.

title: Longitudinal studies - PMC
author: Caruana et al. (2015)
organization: PMC / NIH National Library of Medicine
snippet: Longitudinal studies employ continuous or repeated measures to follow particular individuals over prolonged periods (years/decades). Discusses attrition, scope qualifiers (among participants), and how to interpret correlation vs causation.  OECD long-form 223-page report; country notes, policy analysis, and GDP growth comparisons against the pre-pandemic decade with explicit projection methodology.
notes: Longitudinal cohort methodology; perfect for SCOPE-qualifier parsing.

title: Understanding and misunderstanding randomized controlled trials
author: A Deaton and N Cartwright (2018)
organization: PMC / NIH National Library of Medicine
snippet: Criticises treating ATE from an RCT as truth beyond trial sample. Famous Lalonde (1986) example. Discusses external validity, scope qualifiers, and limitations of causal claims derived from RCTs.  OECD PISA 2022 Vol I; long-form 458-page report; country-level results, equity analysis, methodology appendices, and COVID-19 impact discussion with statistical annex.
notes: Deaton and Cartwright - landmark methodological article on RCT external validity.

title: The reproducibility 'crisis': Reaction to replication failure
author: P Hunter (2017)
organization: PMC / NIH National Library of Medicine
snippet: Discusses reproducibility crisis: if a study results fall just on side of statistical significance, replication has high probability of refuting them. 102+ citations. Tests NEGATIVE-claim and EVIDENCE_LIMITATION parsing.  Full-text PISA report; includes causal-inference section on COVID-19 effects; covers 81 participating countries with sampling weights and codebooks.
notes: Reproducibility-crisis paper; 102+ citations.

title: A full-document analysis of the semantic relation between EPAR and journal articles

PISA microdata; perfect for international comparative analysis with student-level cognitive items, contextual questionnaires, sampling weights, and codebooks for re-analysis.
notes: Direct analysis of EMA EPARs - perfect for testing how regulator language differs from journal language.

title: Potayto - Potahto? The Meaning of the FDA's 'Complete Response Letter'
author: M Senak (2008)
organization: PMC / NIH National Library of Medicine
snippet: Explains that a Complete Response Letter (CRL) states that the FDA cannot approve an NDA in its current form and describes specific deficiencies in the application. Critical for NEGATIVE-claim parsing of regulatory non-approval language.
notes: Explains FDA CRL semantics - useful for parsing regulatory non-approval language.
